t: Kumasi was founded around 1680 as the capital of the Ashanti Empire, and its ruler, the Asantehene, was also ruler of the empire.
The Aowin sacked the city in 1718 and 1719, and the British burnt parts of it in 1874, invaded it again in 1895 and 1896 and ended the war of 1900 with the defeat of the Ashanti by 1 January 1901.
Under British rule from 1901 the city was modernised with railways, a fort, hospitals and colleges, and after Ghana's independence in 1957 it became the capital of the Ashanti Region.
dyk: According to legend, it was at Kumasi that Okomfo Anokye received the Golden Stool, the embodiment of the soul of the Ashanti nation, and the city's name means "under the kum tree".
ev: Osei Kofi Tutu I founds Kumasi as the capital of the Ashanti Empire
Kumasi rises to prominence as the capital of the Ashanti Empire
The Aowin king Ebirimoro invades and sacks Kumasi, and Opoku Ware I beats back the invasion
The British burn parts of the city, including the royal residence, in the Third Anglo-Ashanti War
The British invade Kumasi again and build Fort Kumasi at the centre of the town
The Ashanti besiege Governor Hodgson in the fort until he breaks out on 23 June
The British formally annex Kumasi and its population has fallen to 3000
Ghana becomes independent and Kumasi becomes the capital of the Ashanti Region

f.founded: Around 1680, or in the 1680s, by Asantehene Osei Kofi Tutu I as the capital of the Ashanti Empire; oral accounts differ on how the site was chosen.
f.where: On the eastern slopes of a ridge rising from the marshes of the Nsuben rivers, in a rain forest region near Lake Bosomtwe in the Ashanti Region of Ghana, about 200 kilometres from Accra.
f.known: Capital of the Ashanti Empire; seat of the Asantehene; the Golden Stool; Okomfo Anokye; the British burnings of 1874 and the siege of 1900; the Kejetia Market; kente cloth
f.today: Kumasi is the second largest city in Ghana and the capital of the Ashanti Region, and it remains the seat of the Asantehene.
